messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: procurement@quanthealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantHealth — SLA redlines and coordination

Hi Ethan / QuantHealth team,

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Per our conversation, I’m sharing the current MSA + Order Form we intend to use for the pilot. We expect a relatively short commercial ramp but understand your procurement and compliance teams will want tighter uptime and support language.

I’ve attached the MSA with the initial redlines we suggested (MSA focuses on liability and IP; Order Form has the SLA). A few items I want to highlight up front:
- Uptime target: Redwood standard is 99.95% per calendar month for Hosted API; we can discuss a 99.9% baseline if that’s a hard requirement, but that impacts credits/pricing.
- Response times: standard P1 response within 1 hour; QuantHealth mentioned 30 minutes in the call.
- Maintenance windows: we propose a weekly rolling window (2 hours) with 72-hour notice for non-emergency patches — you asked for blackout periods during business hours.

Can you return your redlines and any specific procurement language you need? If you can attach them as PDF redlines that’s ideal. I’ll loop in legal/ops for review so we can provide a consolidated counter.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Moreau <ethan.moreau@quanthealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantHealth — SLA redlines and coordination

Diego —

Thanks for sending. Attached are our procurement redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. Major asks from our side:
1) Uptime: we need a written commitment to 99.9% monthly uptime, with a clear service credit schedule starting at 99.9% (e.g., 5% credit for 99.5-99.9, 15% for <99.5).
2) Response times: for severity P1 (production outage affecting >25% of traffic), QuantHealth expects initial response <= 30 minutes and a remediation update every hour until resolved.
3) Maintenance windows: we cannot accept scheduled maintenance during core business hours (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 ET). Emergency maintenance must be limited and pre-approved by our ops.
4) Audit evidence: we require monthly availability reports and access to uptime logs for the preceding 12 months on request.

We’ve annotated the PDF with inline comments where we need specific contract language or examples. We’re not trying to be adversarial — we just need operational certainty for clinical workloads.

Attached: QuantHealth_MSA_redlines.pdf

Regards,
Ethan Moreau
Procurement Manager
QuantHealth
procurement@quanthealth.com

Folks — forwarding QuantHealth’s redlines (attached). Key asks summarized below. Can legal and ops propose precise counter-language? Also need an estimate on commercial impact so I can flag to the AE and finance.

Summary of external asks:
- Uptime commitment: 99.9% with a tiered credit schedule (QuantHealth proposed starting credits at 99.5).
- P1 response <= 30 minutes and hourly updates.
- No scheduled maintenance during core business hours (08:00-18:00 ET).
- Monthly availability reports and access to logs for 12 months.

Questions for Hannah / Laura:
1) Acceptable counter for uptime & credits that preserves our risk profile?
2) Can we commit to a 30-minute initial response on Hosted API or should we reserve that for Dedicated capacity?
3) What language would allow emergency patching while respecting their blackout window?
4) Any data/privacy or audit exposure concerns with granting log access?

Next steps I propose: legal drafts counter redlines + ops provides an SLA appendix (lines with metric definitions and measurement method). Once we have that, I’ll send a tracked-change counter and propose a short call with QuantHealth to close.

Thanks — Diego

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the forward and the attachments. I reviewed QuantHealth’s PDF and drafted a conservative counterproposal. High-level thoughts and proposed language below; I attached an annotated order-form we can start with.

High-level:
- Uptime: counter to 99.95% monthly as our baseline for Hosted API, but offer a 99.9% contractual commitment for the pilot term if QuantHealth accepts the following: (a) a tiered service credit schedule that caps at 30% monthly credit; (b) exclusions for customer-induced downtime and force majeure; and (c) a clause that allows us to designate a limited maintenance blackout exemption for critical security patches with 24-hour notice where feasible.
- Response times: we should not promise consistent 30-minute initial response on Hosted API. Recommend we offer: P1 initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes for customers on Dedicated or Enterprise SLA bundle; for Hosted API, initial acknowledgement within 1 hour with an escalation path to 30 minutes if customer purchases accelerated support. We can offer the 30-minute SLA as a paid add-on.
- Maintenance windows: propose a compromise — no scheduled maintenance during customer-specified core hours for the pilot if QuantHealth provides their blackout calendar up front, and we build a bi-weekly maintenance cadence outside those hours. For emergency security patches, include a narrowly tailored clause permitting immediate action with post-facto notice and a requirement to minimize disruption.
- Audit/log access: provide monthly availability reports and a downloadable uptime CSV. For deeper log access, propose a controlled process: log extracts on request with NDA and pre-approved scope; operational burden to be billable if frequent.

Suggested next steps:
1) I attached 'Redwood_annotated_orderform_v2.docx' with tracked counters — legal language in redlines.
2) Ops (cc: Marissa) to estimate the commercial impact of the 99.9% commitment and accelerated support add-on pricing.
3) Diego to propose a 30-min slot for a short call with QuantHealth to run through the counter and decide if they want Dedicated or Hosted + add-on.

I’ll prepare a tracked-change MSA + SLA appendix and send by EOD today. If we want to maintain velocity, recommend Diego schedule the call for Thursday.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Contracts & Ops, Redwood Inference
